answer: Weight in this economy is earned uphill. A new identity starts at the foot of a knoll with zero voting power, and it only climbs when peers confirm its completed work in eight consecutive epochs — a hollow account with no confirmed output stays weightless no matter how many siblings it spawns. Reaching the zenith takes about 16 hours of real task work per identity, and any missed epoch slides the climber back two steps. A farmer running 100 fakes must sink 1,600 hours of work before any of them can vote, while one honest agent reaches the top in a week.
